title: Fix artifact card previews and log loading
summary: Artifact cards now consistently open their preview modal, and text/log artifacts load more reliably when the bounded range request is unavailable.
userVisibleChange: Clicking anywhere on an artifact card opens its modal. Plain text artifact paths are shown as log previews, and log previews retry without a byte range when the server rejects the initial range request.

risks.title: Historical local log paths may be unavailable
risks.mitigation: The modal still opens and reports the unavailable preview state when a referenced local file no longer exists; the source path remains visible.

timeline.title: Locked artifact interaction plan
timeline.summary: Registered and received approval for the artifact log and modal fix plan.

timeline.title: Unified artifact card preview behavior
timeline.summary: Made every artifact card keyboard and pointer interactive, classified plain text artifacts as logs, and added range fallback loading.

timeline.title: Ran regression, build, server, and browser checks
timeline.summary: UI tests, production build, Go tests, and a live artifact-tab browser check passed.

decisions.title: Use the card as the shared preview interaction
decisions.rationale: Artifact types previously exposed modal behavior only through image and log-specific controls, leaving generic cards inert. A shared card-level interaction makes the behavior consistent while preserving direct source links.

decisions.title: Retry range-rejected log previews
decisions.rationale: Some valid or empty artifacts can reject the bounded HTTP range request with 416. Falling back to a normal fetch preserves the preview without removing the bounded fast path for normal responses.

validation.output: TypeScript checking, Vite production build, and embedded UI asset copy passed.
Generic recorded-file and log artifact cards opened their modal from the card body; text content rendered for an available file. Historical /private/tmp log files were correctly reported unavailable.
